modelingNotes: Exact order 1651320000 = HDC HVE 3+2 FS, female screw contact insert, size 4, 3 power + 2 signal + PE. Confirmed by exact-order data sheet (18.02.2026, pp.1 and 3), historical HVE catalogue female screw row (p.2), and RockStar version 2020 female screw row (physical p.132/B.82). This is the insert alone; housings and mating half are separate.

Historical HVE p.2 female arrangement identifies populated contacts 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9. In the printed female diagram, 1/3/5 run down the left and 7/9 down the right; this records that drawing only and is not an installed viewing-direction assertion. Matching these positions against the exact female SCREW arrangement in RockStar B.82 identifies switch/pilot contacts 1 and 5 and operating/power contacts 3, 7 and 9. This role-to-number assignment is a cross-diagram inference; the documents use opposite filled/open-circle conventions. C. and M. are authoring prefixes for cable screw and corresponding female mating contact, not additional stamped labels or a phase assignment.

Five fixed contact conductors C.1–M.1, C.3–M.3, C.5–M.5, C.7–M.7 and C.9–M.9 represent the numbered screw/contact paths through the passive insert. The candidate conformance declares these fixed links for explicit instance jumpers; single-terminal functions and connector metadata never join nets. Pilot contacts remain conductive within one insert; mating sequence does not create an internal relay, bridge between pilot contacts, or permission to connect/disconnect under voltage or load.

PE is one aggregate logical protective-earth endpoint. Exact data-sheet p.3 documents an M4 PE screw connection and p.4/legacy p.2 show earth-marked hardware, but the independently accessible PE clamps, mating/bonding points and frame continuity are not fully enumerated. No single central PE pin, exact PE screw count, C.PE–M.PE conductor, mounting-screw bond or housing bond is asserted. PE is required by library policy for modeled protective-earth use, not a universal manufacturer requirement for every application. An authored PE connection satisfies presence only and does not prove an external earth source or bonding adequacy.

Capabilities remain notes: DIN EN 61984 rated voltage 830 V, UL/CSA 600 V AC/DC, signal contacts 500 V (RockStar B.80), 8 kV impulse and pollution severity 3. No rating.nominal_voltage, AC-only scalar or current scalar is imposed on this passive insert. These conflicting editions/sections are preserved, and conductor, populated pole count and ambient derating must be evaluated for the application.

Exact data-sheet p.3 gives main-contact M3 screws, 0.5–0.55 Nm, AWG20–14 and nominal 0.5–2.5 mm²; its conductor-specific fields also say 4 mm². It gives 9 mm strip length, while RockStar B.80 says 8 mm. Do not resolve these inconsistent preparation fields into a single universal instruction. PE data: M4, 1.2–1.5 Nm, 10 mm strip, AWG20–12 and rated 4 mm². Temperature capability −40…125 °C does not imply full-current operation throughout that range.

The historical phrase lagging earth contacts is not used as a delayed-PE claim. The exact modern data-sheet p.1 specifies two lagging contacts; its p.3 separately counts two signal and three power contacts, and RockStar B.82 distinguishes the two pilot/switch positions from power. The model records the pilot distinction and leaves detailed timing/interlock behavior outside scope. RockStar B.80 prohibits connection/disconnection under live voltage or load.

connectionCoverage.notes: Eleven modeled endpoints: five manufacturer-numbered cable/mating pairs (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) plus one aggregate required PE. Five explicit fixed paths preserve separate numbered contacts; 1/5 are pilot and 3/7/9 power by the documented female diagram comparison. Partial scope: individual PE clamp/mating/bonding interfaces, mounting-frame continuity and external housing bonds are not fully inventoried; aggregate PE is not a physical central pin or an invented split-side bridge. Circuit assignment, mating sequence, external bonding and as-built orientation are outside this insert model.
